To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
food quality was the most important dimension of the restaurant experience and that the relative importance of the other dimensions varied across the day of week and the type of restaurant.

the top box analysis of the six dimensions of the restaurant dining experience, as captured on the DinEX, revealed that food quality is perceived by restaurant patrons as the most important experience dimension.

food quality was the most important restaurant dimension, with the highest top box rating of 82 percent, followed by service quality (79 percent), value for money (77 percent), atmosphere (76 percent), convenience (73 percent), and cleanliness (70 percent).

the development of a new approach to the measurement of restaurant quality, and with an analysis of the relative importance of different dimensions of restaurant quality.
the development of a top box analysis methodology to evaluate the importance of the various experience dimensions in the restaurant industry.
the relative perceived importance customers place on each of the six dimensions of the restaurant dining experience.

the results of this study are consistent with the findings of previous studies in the area, and offer valuable guidance for the restaurant operator in terms of optimizing the restaurant experience.

restaurant operators should focus their attention on food quality and service to ensure a positive dining experience for their customers.

the relative importance of the six DinEX dimensions is not the same for every meal period or restaurant category.
